Subject: Post-demo: latency buckets & deployment path recommendation

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap from our side plus two suggested next steps so you can pick the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity):

Summary from call:
- Workload: user-facing chat for checkout assistance, ~500k monthly active users, peak 1k RPS in short bursts.
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens in, 220 tokens out (median); tail can hit 800 tokens during extended context threads.
- SLO target: p95 <= 120ms for single-turn responses during steady state; acceptable p95 <= 300ms during bursts if fallbacks apply.

Observed signals that matter for deployment choice:
- Sustained concurrency: ~150 concurrent requests in steady windows, with burst spikes up to 1k for ~40-90s.
- Cost sensitivity: want predictable per-month spend; willing to commit to reserved capacity if latency payoff is clear.
- Data isolation: no on-prem requirement; standard SOC2 controls only.

Recommendation (quick):
- Pilot on Dedicated capacity with a burst routing policy to Hosted as a fallback. Dedicated will meet stable p95 < 120ms at your median context (220 tokens out) and reduce token-unit cost.
- Use Hosted for ingest/low-QPS experiments and to handle overflow during 90s spikes.

Two next steps I recommend now:
1) Ben -> send a short latency vs QPS artifact (attached) showing estimated p50/p95 at 150/300/800 QPS on our Dedicated profiles + cost estimate.
2) FastLane -> confirm a target pilot window (2–4 weeks) and identify internal contact for infra runbook/comms.

I attached a compact CSV with modeled latency/QPS rows and a one-page Dedicated cost sketch.

Ben

2) For bursts: if we route overflow to Hosted, what's the expected performance degradation (p95) and is there an automatic retry/failover?

Tom and I will also want a short pilot SOW to hand to legal — can you include a simple statement of work with expected pilot capacity and cancellation terms?

If you can answer 1/2 and drop the SOW draft, we can try to start a pilot the week of Sep 20.

Sofia — thanks for the quick follow-ups. Answers below and attached a one-page SOW draft.

1) Measurement: the CSV I attached models end-to-end p50/p95 including network + generation time for a typical US region hop (app -> Redwood region US-West). Notes:
   - For Dedicated at 150 QPS steady: modeled end-to-end p95 ≈ 95–110ms at median 220-token outputs.
   - At 300 QPS steady: p95 ≈ 150–180ms (still within acceptable range if you expand p95 target slightly).
   - During a 1k QPS 60s burst routed to Hosted fallback: modeled p95 ≈ 420–520ms (higher due to routing + cold-start contention).

2) Hosted fallback behavior: automatic routing policy can overflow requests to Hosted. There is an optional soft-retry policy (2 retries) and an immediate fallback flag if latency crosses your configured threshold. That yields higher reliability but increases observed p95 because of retries. We recommend setting an availability-first fallback for checkout flows (so that responses may be slower but still arrive) and a strict latency-first policy for fraud/authorization flows.

Attached items: latency_qps_summary.csv, redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf, redwood-dedicated-cost-estimate.pdf

Karthik — can you confirm the Dedicated profile we should propose for this pilot (GPU type + expected concurrency per shard)? Marissa — can you own the SOW handoff to FastLane legal once Karthik confirms profile?

Ben

Ben / Sofia — quick confirmation from infra side:

Dedicated recommendation for FastLane pilot:
- GPU profile: 8xA10G (multi-shard, ongoing traffic coalescing)
- Shard sizing: target 150 sustained concurrency per shard; start with 2 shards (handles steady + buffer), autoscale to 4 on 5-minute sustained pressure.
- Expected steady p95: 100–120ms (end-to-end, US-West) at 220-token outputs.
- Burst policy: overflow to Hosted with soft retry disabled by default (we'll enable per-route flags), expected p95 in Hosted overflow ~450ms.

Operational asks for pilot (what we'd need from FastLane):
- Pilot start: 2027-09-20 (2-week pilot, extendable).
- A single infra/ops point of contact for runbook and certificate exchange.
- Test traffic window and a short prompt set for quality regression checks.

Ben / Marissa — I can finalize the capacity numbers in the SOW. Sofia / Tom — if Sept 20 works, we can ship a pilot SOW and a basic runbook by Friday Sep 10.
